steps.body: You already know the break: when a column's top digit is smaller than the one you're subtracting, break 1 from the next place over into 10 of this place. That break is never repaid — it's spent. The same rule works no matter how big the number gets, even when breaks cascade through several places in a row.

widget.prompt: Walk through 524,613 − 178,945 one column at a time.

panels.title: Ones
panels.body: 3 is smaller than 5. Break 1 ten into 10 ones: the tens digit (1) becomes 0, and ones becomes 13. 13 − 5 = 8.

panels.title: Tens
panels.body: The tens digit is now 0, smaller than 4. Break 1 hundred into 10 tens: hundreds (6) becomes 5, tens becomes 10. 10 − 4 = 6.

panels.title: Hundreds
panels.body: Hundreds is now 5, smaller than 9. Break 1 thousand: thousands (4) becomes 3, hundreds becomes 15. 15 − 9 = 6.

panels.title: Thousands
panels.body: Thousands is now 3, smaller than 8. Break 1 ten-thousand: ten-thousands (2) becomes 1, thousands becomes 13. 13 − 8 = 5.

panels.title: Ten-thousands and up
panels.body: Ten-thousands is now 1, smaller than 7. Break 1 hundred-thousand: hundred-thousands (5) becomes 4, ten-thousands becomes 11. 11 − 7 = 4. Finally, 4 − 1 = 3. The answer is 345,668.

widget.continueFeedback: Keep walking through each column, left to right.
widget.successFeedback: 524,613 − 178,945 = 345,668 — five breaks in a row, each one spent and never repaid.

predict.prompt: When a column can't subtract, where does the help come FROM?
predict.reveal: The left neighbor is worth ten of the stuck column — it breaks one of its units into ten smaller ones and lends them over. Help always flows down the place ladder.

explanationVariants: 2 is smaller than 7 in the ones column, so break 1 ten into 10 ones: 12 − 7 = 5. The full answer is 4,565.
The ones, tens, and hundreds columns each need a break here, cascading one into the next.

steps.body: A break can trigger ANOTHER break — the same cascade you saw with adding, run in reverse. Handle one column at a time, right to left, and keep breaking forward whenever the top digit is smaller than the one you're subtracting. The rule never changes; it just repeats.

explanationVariants: 83,251 − 46,378 needs breaks in the ones, tens, hundreds, and thousands columns, landing on 36,873.
Each break feeds the next column's shortage until every column balances.

commonErrors.feedback: 43,127 subtracted the smaller digit from the larger in every column, ignoring which number is on top. Breaking correctly through the cascade gives 36,873.
37,873 is one break short in an early column. Re-checking each column's break gives 36,873.

explanationVariants: A broken digit stays broken for the rest of the problem — it's spent, not repaid.
Once the hundreds digit lends 1 to the tens column, it keeps its lower value.

widget.prompt: The hundreds digit breaks 1 into the tens column. Later, does the hundreds digit get that 1 back?

options.label: No — the break is spent for the rest of the problem
options.feedback: Once broken, a digit keeps its lower value. The break is never repaid.

options.label: Yes — it's returned once the tens column finishes
options.feedback: The hundreds digit stays permanently lower. Breaking is a one-way trade, never returned.

options.label: Yes — but only if the final answer needs it
options.feedback: The break isn't conditional — once made, the hundreds digit is permanently reduced by 1.

options.label: It depends on the numbers being subtracted
options.feedback: It never depends on the numbers — a break always stays spent, no matter what the rest of the problem looks like.

takeaways: When a top digit is smaller than what you're subtracting, break 1 from the next place over into 10 of this place.
A break is spent — it's never repaid, even later in the same problem.
Breaks can cascade — one break can trigger another, and another.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **When a top digit is too small, break 1 from the next place into 10 of this place — spent, never repaid.** For 52 − 27: ones 2 is smaller than 7, so break the tens (5→4), ones becomes 12. 12 − 7 = 5, then 4 − 2 = 2. Result: 25.
